title: I Raised My Face to the Sky…
text:
I raised my face to the sky,

an immense stone of weathered letters:

the stars revealed nothing to me.
editorial_note: The sky is read as an eroded inscription rather than a source of revelation; weathered keeps both age and exposure to the elements.

title: Lady
text:
Every night she descends into the well

and in the morning reappears

with a new reptile in her arms.
editorial_note: The mythic descent and unexplained reptile remain starkly literal; no identity is imposed upon the poem’s archetypal lady.

title: Epitaph for a Poet
text:
He wished to sing, to sing

so as to forget

his true life made of lies

and remember

his lying life made of truths.
editorial_note: The mirrored paradoxy of verdadera, mentiras, mentirosa, and verdades is kept structurally exact, with song suspended between forgetting and memory.

title: The Scream, the Beak, the Tooth, the Howls…
text:
The scream, the beak, the tooth, the howls,

butcher nothingness and all its racket,

before this simple flower fade away.
editorial_note: Carnicera remains the compact compound butcher nothingness; violence and noise grammatically dissolve before the flower’s simplicity.

title: Here
text:
My footsteps on this street
echo
on another street
where
I hear my footsteps
passing on this street
where


Only the fog is real.
editorial_note: The repeated street and suspended where preserve the spatial loop; the fog’s reality arrives only after syntax and footsteps lose their bearings.

title: Born from Me, from My Shadow…
text:
Born from me, from my shadow,

it dawns across my skin,

daybreak of drowsy light.


A wild dove is your name,

timid upon my shoulder.
editorial_note: The unnamed presence is allowed to shift between dawn, body, and name; brava becomes wild while its dove remains tenderly timid.

title: My Footsteps on This Street…
text:
My footsteps on this street

echo

on another street

where

I hear my footsteps

passing on this street

where


Only the fog is real.
editorial_note: This separately sourced witness of “Here” receives the same reviewed wording while preserving its expanded stanza spacing and first-line title.

title: Daybreak
text:
Swift cold hands

remove one by one

the bandages of shadow


I open my eyes

still

I am alive

at the center

of a still-fresh wound.
editorial_note: Todavía is first temporal and then adjectival through still and still-fresh; waking becomes survival inside the wound opened by dawn.
